587.q: Well let’s not forget Thelonious Monk. That’s a whole ‘nother category by itself. Because not only was he the underpinnings harmonically for modern jazz, but he was musical theater at the same time. I mean you couldn’t make him up, you can’t make that up you know, because I got a chance to actually…

221.s: Reacting to Rowe's name, he recalls Thelonious Monk coming to hear him at the Trident and says Monk took 'Blue Monk' from McShann.
221.q: He was a big fan of mine, well we were fans of each other. And when I played and I used to play at the Trident, in Sausalito, he and his wife would come over. As a matter of fact

588.t: Monk: 'Don't be so perfect' at the Straight Ahead session
588.s: Monk told her not to be perfect; she recalls the Candid session with Hawkins, Booker Little, Mal Waldron, and Max.
588.q: Yeah. We are perfect. Who's so smart that they could say that this is imperfect? Compared to what? It's perfect. Got cracks and holes in it and it's perfect. Thelonius Monk said to me once at this session, "Don't be so perfect." He meant -- I said to Max, "You know what Thelonius said to me? He…

141.t: A month at the Five Spot with Monk, left out of the biography
141.s: He played a month with Monk and tries to recall the drummer, perhaps Ben Riley.
141.q: I was left out of Monk’s biography. I played a gig with him at the Five Spot for a month, and it was left out of the biography.

490.t: Paying for his own concerts; Monk staying in his bed
490.s: Jim Harrison taught him not to expect money from concerts; he recalls Monk living with him for ten years and playing the Carnegie Hall concert.
490.q: don’t have to account nothing to myself. I’m not going to say, “What did I do with that last penny?” You know, so I’d save my money, give the concert – never make any money. I learned that a long time ago. I learned that from a friend of mine named Jim Harrison. Once he told me, he said, “Barry,…

417.t: Opening for Thelonious Monk at the Village Vanguard
417.s: Monk talks to him in the kitchen dressing room about Charlie Christian and arriving in New York, and they later tour together.
417.q: No, but that was another club that I liked too. We opened for him down at the Village Vanguard. He used to talk to me in the kitchen. That was the dressing room, really, the big kitchen they had.

133.t: Thelonious Monk: personal relationship and Walton's take on his music
133.s: Monk admired pianists and told Walton to play his own stuff; Walton says he tries to extend what Monk left out.
133.ch: Piano influences and the Hard Bop label
133.q: Yeah, well I tried … perhaps I'm guilty of tryin' to enlarge on it or, uh, you know, develop it, you know, what he left out, maybe. You know, I don't know exactly uh, how to explain that, but uh, it's almost impossible in my view to not be attracted to Thelonious Monk, his style, magnificent,…

101.s: How Orrin Keepnews put Monk on Terry's Riverside date and the night at Nica's apartment.
101.q: The old man. I felt very flattered to have been one of the – still feel very flattered to be one of the few people that Monk recorded with as a sideman. He – there’s very few records on the scene except the one that he did with me and Art Blakey as a sideman. He never bothered to do it. He was so…

515.s: Corea describes learning Monk through Roy Haynes, hearing Monk's quartet, and trying to keep the composer in the playing.
515.q: I always loved what Monk did. I guess it was a little bit later on that I started to try to interpret and play Monk’s music. Then certainly, when I met Roy... Roy was one of the great Monk drummers, and Roy loved, and loves, Monk. So when I’d hang out with Roy, Roy would talk about Monk and... And…

470.t: Thelonious Monk at the Five Spot and the Cincinnati ballpark
470.s: Monk said Baker looked like him in 1962 and, two years later in Cincinnati, that Baker was uglier; Baker also begins describing his early cello struggles.
470.ch: A broken jaw and the switch to cello
470.q: I’m not sure he liked the writing all that much, but it was part of filling up what the band had to do. So, we played that. And, oh, I’ve got to tell you one of the funniest stories I can ever remember. When we were in the Five Spot the first time – [the] Five Spot was owned by the Termini…

527.t: Teddy Charles as a person and his Monk influence
527.s: Charles sought something more advanced than vibes mainstream, inspired chiefly by Monk, and later ran a yacht.
527.q: No, the only thing that I can say basically was that he was trying to find another area. He was content just playing the vibes like Milt Jackson or Lionel Hampton. He wanted to do something that was more advanced. There was no audience for it … He’s not in music now. He’s has a yacht. He rents the…

491.t: Thelonious Monk and Coltrane's time in his group
491.s: Golson describes Monk's seemingly childlike tunes, the one night Monk seemed down to earth, hearing him at Minton's, and Monk calling out Coltrane's name.
491.q: Monk. He was known as that crazy guy that plays that funny piano and writes those crazy tunes. Now there’s a Thelonious . . .

589.t: First impressions of Monk and Bud Powell
589.s: He first thought Monk could not play, but learned to understand him; Bud Powell also came slowly.
589.q: The very first time I heard Monk, I didn’t think he knew how to play the piano. The very first time I heard Monk, I thought he hadn’t practiced very well. But you have to learn to understand Monk. Monk does not come easily. Once you understand and appreciate him, you end up owning most of his CDs,…

104.t: Visitors at the Hickory House: Oscar Pettiford, Wilbur Ware and Monk
104.s: Oscar Pettiford taught her his tunes, Wilbur Ware came in poor shape, and Monk came after she invited him, listened silently and left her the check.
104.q: “Swinging ’Til the Girls Come Home.” We used to play all those tunes with him. Another guy who would come in, but he would come in in not terribly good shape, Wilbur Ware. What a fine bass player he was.

506.t: Subbing for Sam Jones with Thelonious Monk
506.s: Carter fills in with Monk at Circle in the Square and in Philadelphia while commuting to school.
506.q: Yes, he had the flu or something and I get a call – I can't remember who called me – they said that Sam is sick tonight and could I do this concert at the Circle in the Square which was right across from the Village Gate. It's a theater, a small theater. And I said, "Yeah." So I went over to the…

219.t: The Giants of Jazz tour and Dizzy and Monk
219.s: Wein describes the cooperative 1971 tour and why Dizzy and Monk did not relate musically.
219.q: Well, you know, as big as they were, there was not that much work for them, so … and I'll never forget them because whenever I took Thelonious or Dizzy, they flew first class. But when we did this tour, they all agreed to fly tourist class, which I couldn't believe it, but they, you know, they were…

1.t: Thelonious Monk's tricks on bass players
1.s: Danny says Monk counts in the middle of tunes and breaks the rules to throw bassists.
1.ch: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
1.q: See, when you sit next to piano players and you get to analyzing who is great and who ain't, Thelonious Monk is counting like crazy, but he's trying to throw you, because his purpose was to get popular with the new things that was supposed to have been unorthodox. So of course, in the turnaround,…

377.t: A duo record with Freddie Green; Monk
377.s: Basie jokes about a record with only Freddie Green, and says a duo needs a rhythm section, and that nobody plays like Monk.
377.q: Stop putting me with these champions. listen here, I've got enough to fool with this tiger I mean, (unintelligible) tag I'm with. this tiger, Yeah, Freddie Green.

66.t: Monk falls asleep in her apartment
66.s: Monk once entered her apartment and lay down in the other bed; her scream sent him into the closet. She says Monk replayed new tunes for months to see if they stuck.
66.ch: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
66.q: When the guys left the door was open and Monk rang the doorbell and he came inside. He discovered that I was asleep - it was around 8 o'clock in the morning. I had a big, big twin bed, so when I woke up I saw something on the other bed and I screamed. He yelled too and ran out the door and ran in…

166.t: Why you couldn't follow Monk: closing his ears
166.s: Monk played against the meter; Simmons listened to Milt Jackson instead.
166.ch: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
166.q: Yes. Well, working with Monk, you couldn't follow him. He played between the keys, he played against the meter, and he would just play all over the piano, you know. It wasn't anything you could follow. If you didn't know the tune, you couldn't play with him. Now, if you're playing by ear, you had…

168.t: Working with Thelonious Monk at Newport in 1964
168.s: His one time with Monk was a festival jam set at Newport in 1964, where Monk played his own modern ideas.
168.q: Yes, I worked with Thelonius. The first time I actually worked with him was at the Newport Jazz Festival. I worked with him on one of the sets, you know, and this took place in 1964.

388.t: Monk's disastrous rehearsal and the end of Dixieland
388.s: Thelonious Monk comes to the rehearsal and it goes badly, so Kenny Kersey is hired; Ben drops the Dixieland charts after two sets and the band just plays jazz.
388.q: However, I have to say first, as we went to the rehearsal, he hadn't hired Kenny yet, and we rehearsed first without Kenny and somebody suggested that Monk --Thelonius Monk -- was at Minton's and he was out for awhile and he could use a job.

78.s: Horace never saw Monk play but respects him as a creator from what musicians say.
78.ch: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
78.q: Unfortunately, I don't know too much about Thelonius Monk, except I've read a little something about him, and I've never seen him play. I've heard one or two of his recordings, but they were interesting, and I've heard musicians that play in my group talk about him. And they respected him, you…

529.s: Monk calls Sam, refuses to rehearse, and Charlie Rouse says to keep bugging him; Monk's extra bars are hard.
529.q: So when I was down there, checking in at home, and uh, and they said a man called here named Thelonius Monk, for you. We told him that you would be back next week, and he said get in touch with him as soon as you get back. I say Thank Goodness, I will. I'm jumping out of the frying pan into the pot…
